title: Finding a Seat at a Coffee Shop
setting: The coffee shop is crowded, and you ask whether the empty seat next to someone is available.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hey, do you know if this seat's taken?
dialogue.zh: 嗨，你知道这个座位有人吗？

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: No, go ahead. I'm just waiting for my drink.
dialogue.zh: 没有，你坐吧。我只是在等我的饮料。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Thanks. It's packed in here today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I know. I almost turned around when I saw the line.
dialogue.zh: 就是啊。我看到排队那么长，差点直接掉头走了。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Same. I figured I'd give it a few minutes and see if it moved.
dialogue.zh: 我也是。我想着先等几分钟，看看队伍会不会往前走。

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Good call. It actually went pretty fast.
dialogue.zh: 这决定不错。其实队伍走得还挺快的。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Yeah, no worries. I wasn't in a huge rush anyway.
dialogue.zh: 是啊，没事。反正我也不是特别赶时间。

expressions.note: One of the most natural ways to ask about an empty seat.
Very common for restaurants, stores, bars, trains, and events.
Casual and common in everyday American conversation.

expressions.zh: 好主意 / 这个决定不错。
expressions.note: Used to approve of someone's choice or judgment.
A high-frequency phrase: I'm kind of in a rush.

exercise: You enter a crowded coffee shop and see an empty seat next to me. Say 2–3 natural English sentences: ask whether the seat is taken, comment that the place is packed, and mention that you're not in a big rush.
